examples.problem_statement: Multiply 85 × 98 using the Nikhilam base method

solution.operation: Choose the base 100
solution.description: Both numbers are near this power of 10, so Nikhilam applies

solution.operation: Write the deviations from the base
solution.description: Deviation = number − base

solution.operation: Cross-add for the left part
solution.description: Either cross-sum gives the same left part

solution.operation: Multiply the deviations for the right part
solution.description: The right part occupies 2 digits — the width of the base's zeros

solution.operation: Assemble the answer
solution.description: left \times 100 + right, with the digits placed by width

common_mistakes: forgetting the carry when the deviation product overflows the base digits
sign error when one deviation is positive and one negative

examples.problem_statement: Square 655 using Ekadhikena Purvena (one more than the previous)

solution.operation: Split off the final 5
solution.description: The sutra applies to any number whose last digit is 5

solution.operation: Take one more than the previous digits
solution.description: 'Ekadhikena Purvena' means by one more than the previous one

solution.operation: Multiply the previous by that successor
solution.description: This product forms the left-hand part of the square

solution.operation: Append 25
solution.description: The square of the final 5 always contributes exactly 25

common_mistakes: multiplying the digits by themselves instead of by the next number
